source_ref: OSF dqw9f (public node; API reports no node licence), Supplemental Studies/Study S1c Data and Code/Study S1c Data.sav (https://osf.io/download/2knxu/, sha256 4a5debaf...d9142e) and Supplemental Studies/Study S2c Data and Code/Study S2c Data.sav (https://osf.io/download/6501f901f3dcd16832ddd406/, sha256 77e72d25...e4732e) -- SPSS variable and value labels of apply1/apply2; data/wallace_2026_mindsets.py for the code derivation and the S2c recode. Paper: Wallace, Murphy, Hernandez-Colmenares & Fujita (2026) JPSP 130(2) 291-307, doi:10.1037/pspi0000498.
note: Level 1, both label levels read. Code derivation: item IS the source column name (apply1, apply2 in both .sav files; the script maps apply{i}->apply{i}), so exempt from Step 5b and no verification files. PER-STUDY VARIANTS: the same code carries different wording by study (live cov_study 4 = S1c, 796 ids; 7 = S2c, 793 ids). S1c's labels name MCM Consulting/the consulting industry; S2c's name XYZ Organization/volunteering. The schema allows one item_text per item and a duplicate item row per study would break the item/resp join (dup_item_resp), so, following SKILL.md's counterbalanced-design rule, item_text carries BOTH verbatim labels, each prefixed with 'Study S1c (cov_study = 4): ' / 'Study S2c (cov_study = 7): ' and joined by ' | '. The prefixes and separator are IRW's, not the source's; the wording after each prefix is the variable label verbatim, including the source's own typo 'how likely would to be to submit' in apply2 of both studies, not corrected. OPTIONS: S1c value labels are 1='1 - not at all' ... 7='7 - very much'; S2c's run the other way (1='1 - very much' ... 7='7 - not at all'), and the processing script rewrote S2c as 8-resp (itemcov_recoded=1 on all 1586 S2c rows). Live counts confirm this cell for cell (route 9): S1c apply1 41/32/48/93/169/203/210 source = live; S2c apply1 source 1..7 = 98/126/160/121/83/88/117, live 1..7 = 117/88/83/121/160/126/98 (exact reversal); apply2 likewise (S1c 42/33/50/94/156/187/234; S2c source 105/129/161/105/78/84/131 -> live reversed). So in the live table resp 1 = not at all and 7 = very much for BOTH studies; option_text ships those two anchors with the source's '1 - '/'7 - ' number prefixes stripped (they would be wrong for the recoded S2c rows). resp 2-6 are labelled only with their own digit in the source and are left blank, not padded. No instructions text exists in either .sav; left blank. Rights: study-authored items, no stated restriction located (silence = permission). Incidental: the script's docstring says XYZ Organization was used in S1c, but S1c's own labels name MCM Consulting throughout (MCMmanip1-4R, interest1-3, learn1-3, apply1-2, rec1-2); docstring defect only, the data are unaffected.
public_note: The two items were worded differently in the two pooled studies (a consulting firm, MCM Consulting, in Study S1c, cov_study = 4; a volunteer organization, XYZ Organization, in Study S2c, cov_study = 7), so item_text gives both wordings labelled by study; responses are coded 1 = not at all to 7 = very much in both studies, Study S2c having been reverse-recoded from its printed order (itemcov_recoded = 1).
